outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Chip-design and AI-infrastructure software, led by Synopsys and Arm
strongest.reason: Synopsys' blowout fiscal Q3 beat and Arm's continued AI/AGI CPU momentum reinforced confidence that AI-driven design complexity keeps fueling this corner of the market even amid broader semiconductor-tariff uncertainty

strongest.area: Foundry and memory chipmakers, led by Micron and TSMC
strongest.reason: both extended gains as AI-chip demand signals stayed resilient, with Micron shrugging off tariff jitters and TSMC continuing to draw fund rotation from weaker names

weakest.area: AI software and government-facing tech, led by Palantir and ServiceNow
weakest.reason: Palantir fell sharply after Google DeepMind's new cybersecurity AI model raised competitive concerns for its core government business, while ServiceNow and other enterprise software names gave back a slice of their recent multi-month run

weakest.area: Consumer-facing AI disruption plays, led by Adobe
weakest.reason: Adobe sank on a CEO-succession announcement just ahead of earnings, with analysts sharply divided over whether AI substitution poses a structural threat to its Creative Cloud franchise

outlook.nextStep: The August inflation report due September 11 and the September 15-16 FOMC decision are now the key catalysts worth tracking closely, since Fed-funds odds have been swinging on nearly every official's comment. Company-specific moves like Tesla's Cybercab/NHTSA headline and Adobe's leadership transition are probably better watched for follow-through over the next week than acted on based on a single day's price swing.

signals.title: Fed rate-hike odds firm back up ahead of key inflation report
signals.body: Prediction markets and Fed-funds futures show odds of a 25-basis-point hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting swinging widely, roughly 50-65% depending on the source, moving on every new Fed comment. Governor Waller said the August inflation report due September 11 will be the key input for his own vote.
signals.focus: the single most important date on the calendar this month worth tracking closely; day-to-day comment-driven swings are probably better watched than traded on

signals.title: Tesla's Cybercab event draws a regulatory probe and investor disappointment
signals.body: Tesla's invite-only Cybercab showcase left deployment numbers and locations unanswered, and the event wasn't livestreamed. NHTSA has since opened an audit query into whether the vehicle's self-certification met federal safety standards, compounding the post-event stock slide.
signals.focus: a regulatory-risk headline worth watching for NHTSA's findings rather than reacting to a single day's move

signals.title: Adobe names new CEO days ahead of earnings, drawing a mixed analyst reaction
signals.body: Adobe tapped Anil Chakravarthy to succeed longtime CEO Shantanu Narayen effective December 1, adding a leadership-transition question mark just before next week's fiscal Q3 report. Analysts are split: Morgan Stanley downgraded the stock on AI-substitution risk to Creative Cloud, while Barclays and RBC raised their price targets.
signals.focus: a genuine fork in analyst opinion worth watching resolve at next week's earnings rather than reacting to the transition headline alone

signals.title: Google DeepMind's new cybersecurity AI model pressures Palantir
signals.body: Google DeepMind unveiled Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, a purpose-built model for vulnerability detection and automated patching aimed at government and enterprise clients. Palantir shares fell sharply on the announcement despite separately landing a new Army TITAN contract.
signals.focus: a competitive-threat headline worth watching for follow-through rather than a reason to react to one day's selloff

signals.title: Synopsys jumps on strong AI-driven chip-design demand
signals.body: Synopsys beat fiscal Q3 estimates with sales up 42.5% year-over-year, driven by what management called unprecedented complexity in AI chip design. The stock posted one of its largest single-day gains in over a year.
signals.focus: a fundamentally strong quarter worth watching for how the stock holds its gains over the next few sessions

signals.title: Crypto gives back gains as rate-hike odds firm and Ethereum ETFs see outflows
signals.body: Bitcoin pulled back from its four-month high near $82,000 into the mid-$70,000s as rate-hike expectations for the September Fed meeting firmed up. Ethereum underperformed further, with ETH ETFs seeing net outflows even as Bitcoin ETFs took in modest inflows.
signals.focus: a reminder of how sensitive crypto remains to Fed rate expectations; probably better watched through the September 16 decision than traded on daily swings

signals.title: Semiconductor tariff uncertainty persists alongside broad AI-chip strength
signals.body: Commerce Secretary Lutnick reiterated that targeted semiconductor tariffs are coming, with rates and exemptions still undecided. Despite that overhang, most chip names (AMD, TSM, Micron, ASML, Arm) rallied on resilient AI-driven demand signals.
signals.focus: a slow-moving policy risk that's probably better tracked for concrete tariff details than traded on day-to-day headlines
